caption: The drawing displays two views of a woodwind instrument, most likely a flute or fife, depicted horizontally on a plain, light beige background. The top half of the drawing presents a shaded, realistic rendering of the instrument in gray and brown tones, showing subtle woodgrain texture. The instrument features a slightly bulging mouthpiece with an oval opening, followed by a cylindrical body containing six evenly spaced finger holes and a defined ring near the end. The lower half of the drawing presents a black line diagram of the same instrument, oriented in the same direction. This diagram emphasizes contour lines and key measurements, including two labeled distances—5 inches from the mouthpiece to the beginning of the finger holes and 7½ inches for the main length with holes. There are additional notes specifying a ¾ inch diameter at the mouthpiece end and ½ inch at the other end. The diagram also marks the location and profile of the holes along the body, matching the finger holes seen in the shaded drawing above. Both views are placed on a plain background without additional decorative elements.
title: Wooden Fife
